purpose: Replace an unhandled throw in resolvePrNumber()'s NaN guard with core.setFailed() + return null so non-numeric pr-number input degrades gracefully instead of causing an unhandled promise rejection. Also flags duplicate unguarded parsing in review.ts for follow-up.
riskRationale: Minimal, targeted change to a single guard clause in a single file. All three callers already check for null. The function contract is preserved and strengthened. No new code paths or dependencies introduced.

text: The PR correctly aligns the NaN guard in resolvePrNumber() with its Promise<number | null> contract by replacing throw new Error with core.setFailed() + return null. The sanitize() wrapper around user-controlled input follows established patterns and prevents log injection. The fix is minimal, well-scoped, and correctly addresses issue #184. A secondary finding reveals that review.ts duplicates the pr-number parsing logic without the same NaN guard.

reasoning: The change is correct, aligns with the function contract, all callers handle null gracefully, and sanitize() is properly applied. No regressions expected. The review.ts duplication is a related concern but falls outside the scope of this PR.

message: The NaN guard now correctly aligns with the function's Promise<number | null> return type contract — throwing was a contract violation that caused an unhandled rejection.
The sanitize() wrapper around the user-controlled prNumberInput prevents log injection (Bearer tokens, GitHub tokens, etc.), consistent with all other core.setFailed() calls in this file.
return null is the correct degraded value — all three callers check for null before proceeding, so the fix naturally integrates with existing error paths.

review.ts has duplicate inline pr-number parsing logic that also lacks a NaN guard after parseInt(). A non-numeric pr-number in review mode silently passes NaN to gh.getPR(NaN), which will fail with a confusing API error instead of a clear message.
suggestion: Extract resolvePrNumber() into a shared utility (e.g. action/src/utils.ts) and call it from both fix.ts and review.ts, or add the same NaN guard to review.ts's inline parsing logic.
